term: difference of nature, difference in act, and limitation
resolution: Three things are kept apart. A difference in act is opposite truth values of the supplied InAct at one respect. A difference of nature is inequality of represented essence values, and may hold where act profiles coincide. A limiting principle is composition, esse other than essence, or another being prior. No step treats a difference of nature as a limiting principle or as a difference in act: those are the two open conditions UnlimitedBeingsShareNature and FirstMoverActDeterminesNature, each stated as a premise or as a side of an equivalence. Numerical identity comes only through Q11 individuation and the first-mover adapter.
